title: Two first-class interfaces with a shared design and review loop

nodes.summary: Web for humans and MCP for agents are equal product surfaces
nodes.detail: Web (meaning, design, examples, review) and MCP (technical construction, editing, repeatable execution) are equally important first-class surfaces sharing concrete objects (KB, workspace, candidate, example, diagnostic, artifact, feedback), with no mandatory conversation platform.

realised.evidence: kyyn-v2 has only a CLI surface (host/kyyn-surfaces/Cli.hs); no Web or MCP adapter exists by the end of history

nodes.summary: Agent builds evolution to Ready; human reviews and accepts
nodes.detail: The initial authoring workflow: an agent creates a workspace, populates its evolution binding, trials it and marks it Ready; the human inspects changes, outputs, checks and rationale, requests revisions and may accept. These are workflow expectations, not role-based permissions.

realised.evidence: Workspace creation (seq 31), candidate checking (seq 36) and Ready/accept lifecycle (PR #42) exist through the CLI, not yet through Web/MCP

deliveries.evidence: PR #32 creates draft evolution workspaces; trial, Ready and acceptance still missing
PR #37 persists and checks evaluated candidates; Ready lifecycle and acceptance still missing
PR #39 adds Ready/Draft lifecycle operations; acceptance follows in #42

nodes.summary: No graphical evolution-source authoring or helper-launch catalogue
nodes.detail: Parity means shared review objects and operations, not a GUI for every source operation: no helper-launch catalogue, argument-to-source generator or separate invocation model; typed query/example forms remain data interfaces.

realised.evidence: Negative constraint; nothing of the kind exists in code

nodes.summary: No Kyyn task/inbox object; Kyyn never orchestrates the agent
nodes.detail: Requests for new work before an evolution exists go to the user's agent, not a Kyyn task or inbox; examples and review notes support feedback without orchestrating the responding agent, and agent-less preparation conveniences are not required.

realised.evidence: Negative constraint; no task/inbox or agent-orchestration objects exist

nodes.summary: Review notes stored in EvolutionStore against captured work or results
nodes.detail: addReviewNote attaches free-text feedback to a fixed ReviewSubject (captured work, even uncompilable, or an exact evaluated candidate) and a meaningful ReviewTarget (whole, fact, example, source span, artifact); notes are not executable instructions and need no separate approval/ticket subsystem.

realised.evidence: No ReviewSubject/ReviewTarget/addReviewNote code appears in anchors or kyyn-v2

nodes.summary: Typed data examples saved into workspace, distinct from free-text notes
nodes.detail: Executable examples name a query with typed arguments/expected results (buildable as Web forms), saved via saveExample into the workspace's target/examples, which marks it Draft and requires re-checking; they become root material on acceptance.

realised.evidence: Typed query examples and root validation against them land in PR #28; an EvolutionStore saveExample that marks the workspace Draft is not present

nodes.summary: Review shows fact, output, source and check diffs with step report
nodes.detail: Review presents fact/schema differences, view-output differences, KB source changes and changed/removed checks, alongside the ordered step report pairing changed records with declared rationale and evidence; reviewer notes never become evidence.

realised.evidence: CLI `evolution show` presents step reports (seq 33/54) and plugin changes (seq 121), but there is no review surface with view-output or source/check comparisons

deliveries.evidence: PR #34 derives ordered per-fact step reports with rationale and evidence; no review presentation yet
PR #44 shows a workspace's evolution report through the CLI; view-output, source and check comparisons still missing
PR #157 shows plugin source changes in saved evolution reports; view-output and check comparisons still missing

nodes.summary: recordHistory reads per-record timeline from Git and archived reports
nodes.detail: recordHistory over EvolutionStore returns revision-fixed, newest-first RecordHistoryEntry values (recorded change with optional rationale, or unannotated Git diff), stating gaps rather than inventing lineage; no new provenance service or archived-code execution.

realised.evidence: No recordHistory or RecordHistoryEntry code exists

nodes.summary: Previews pinned to base/result; acceptance revision-checked from any client
nodes.detail: Both surfaces identify the base and evaluated result a preview shows; edits or rebases need fresh checks. Acceptance is an explicit operation on a checked evolution conditional on Before.revision matching head, regardless of client, with no authority hierarchy or cross-client editing coordinator.

realised.evidence: Persisted candidates (PR #37) and acceptance checked against Before (PR #42) exist via CLI

deliveries.evidence: PR #37 pins persisted candidates to their captured base and evaluated result; revision-checked acceptance follows in #42

editorial.note: Reconciliation: frontmatter/status cleanup, 'proposed' dropped from the ADR 0010 layout reference, and the MCP table cell 'stable paging' reworded to 'identified collection reads' following the whole-collection-read decision owned elsewhere

notes: This lane is almost static: founded at seq 1 and only touched by the seq 143 reconciliation, so it is effectively a statement of intent that the code has barely reached. The headline commitment (Web and MCP as equal first-class surfaces) is unrealised: the only surface in kyyn-v2 is the CLI. Review notes and recordHistory have no code at all. What is realised is the CLI-level substrate the ADR assumes: evolution workspaces, Ready/accept lifecycle, Before-revision-checked acceptance, persisted step reports and typed query examples. The one substantive wording change at seq 143 (MCP 'stable paging' to 'identified collection reads') quietly drops a pagination expectation; treated as editorial because the owning decision lives in another ADR. Split judgement: with no ### subsections, the Decision was split into nine commitments; the 'Boundaries and alternatives' section (thin transport adapters over shared operations, Web/MCP never calling each other, notifications not canonical state) was treated like an alternatives/consequences section and produced no node, consistent with 0015's 'Alternatives and consequences'.
